extracted.intended_audience: users learning MetaPost for creating technical/vector graphics (students, TeX/LaTeX users, graphics programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for writing MetaPost programs to create vector graphics: control structures, path and transformation operations, styling (pens, dashing, colours), macros, and advanced path manipulations. Includes syntax, examples, and notes on common pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counted for loop syntax and variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic form: for counter = start step stepsize until finish : loop text endfor; The counter is incremented by stepsize until it passes finish. You may use upto as shorthand for step 1 until, and downto for step -1 until.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use counted for loops for unconditional repetition. You can also use for loops to iterate over sequences of expressions separated by commas. Nesting is allowed but each for must be matched by an endfor. Example variants: for i=0 upto xmax: ... endfor; for i=10 downto 1: ... endfor;

rubrics_metrics.name: Using for loops to build up a single statement (path construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: A for loop can be used so that the input lines within it are pieces of a single statement (e.g., pieces of a path definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mode makes the preprocessor accumulate parts of a path: e.g., pts_f := (xmin*ux,log(f(xmin))*uy) for x=xmin+xinc step xinc until xmax: .. (x*ux,log(f(x))*uy) endfor; Use this to construct graphs where each loop iteration appends to the same path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dash pattern and dashing syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: General syntax: draw path dashed dash pattern; dashpattern's argument is a sequence of on/off distances (e.g., on 6bp off 2bp on 2bp off 2bp). Predefined patterns include evenly and withdots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define patterns with dashpattern(on ... off ...). Predefined examples: withdots = dashpattern(off 2.5 on 0 off 2.5); evenly = dashpattern(on 3 off 3). You may scale and shift dash patterns (e.g., dashed dd scaled 2 or dashed evenly scaled 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour specification (RGB) and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The color data type is a triple (r,g,b) with each component between 0 and 1. Use withcolor colour expression in drawing/filling statements. Predefined colours: red=(1,0,0); green=(0,1,0); blue=(0,0,1); black=(0,0,0); white=(1,1,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shades of gray: multiply white by a scalar between 0 and 1. Use withcolor in draw/fill statements and in drawoptions. Examples include creating RGB charts with fill sqr ... withcolor (i*0.1, j*0.1,0); and drawing greyscales via i*0.1*white.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifying the drawing pen
rubrics_metrics.description: Use draw path withpen pen expression to use a specific pen for one draw; use pickup pen expression to set the pen for subsequent draw statements. The default pen is circular with diameter 0.5bp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change thickness with pencircle scaled numeric_expression. Create elliptical/rotated pens via xscaled/yscaled/rotated on pencircle (e.g., pickup pencircle xscaled 2bp yscaled 0.25bp rotated 60). Create shaped pens using makepen(path) (e.g., triangular pen) and use withpen or pickup to apply them.

rubrics_metrics.name: drawoptions to set default drawing style
rubrics_metrics.description: The function drawoptions allows changing default settings for drawing, e.g., drawoptions(dashed evenly withcolor red);
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All draw statements inherit drawoptions settings unless explicitly overridden. Reset drawoptions by calling drawoptions(); beginfig automatically performs grouping that resets options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformations: operators and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Built-in operators: shifted, rotated, rotatedaround, slanted, scaled, xscaled, yscaled, zscaled. rotated(θ) rotates θ degrees counter-clockwise about the origin; rotatedaround(p,θ) rotates about point p. zscaled(a,b) maps (1,0) to (a,b) and can rotate+scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transformations correspond to affine matrices; define a transform variable three ways: (1) composition of basic transformations (e.g., identity shifted ... rotated ...), (2) by specifying the sextuple (Tx,Ty,Txx,Txy,Tyx,Tyy) via xpart/yypart etc., (3) by specifying images of three points. Use inverse(T) to get inverse transform. Use transforms to create reusable graphics and to apply multiple different transformations to the same picture (examples given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection operators: intersectionpoint and intersectiontimes
rubrics_metrics.description: intersectionpoint returns an intersection point of two (possibly curved) paths. intersectiontimes returns the parameter times (t1,t2) at which paths intersect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intersectionpoint for both straight and curved line intersections (e.g., draw (0.5,0)*u -- vline0.5 intersectionpoint pts_f;). intersectiontimes is useful for extracting parameter value 'a' used with subpath to split paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: buildcycle behaviour for joining paths
rubrics_metrics.description: buildcycle(p1, p2, ..., pn) attempts to piece given paths together to form a cyclic path; when multiple intersections exist, it chooses the intersection between each pi and pi+1 to be as late as possible on pi and as early as possible on pi+1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer arranging path arguments so consecutive ones have a unique intersection. buildcycle is useful for creating closed boundaries for filling/shading (example: fill buildcycle(hline0, vline0.5, pts_f, vline4) withcolor ...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clipping a picture to a path
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clip picture_variable to path_expression to restrict a picture to the area inside a cyclic path and discard the outside part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to shade or mask parts of a picture. Example shows building a cycle via buildcycle and then clip currentpicture to c5; after which subsequent drawing operations are clipped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paths as cubic Bézier chains and parametric path operations
rubrics_metrics.description: A path is a chain of cubic Bézier segments. Points on a path are given by p(t) with parameter t in [0,n) for n arcs. Use point t of path, length(path), subpath (pair of times) of path, and arclength/arctime to work with arc lengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: point t of path gives the point; subpath(t1,t2) gives portion from point t1 to t2 (if t1>t2 runs backward). length(path) returns number of arcs. arclength(path) returns arc length; arctime a of p gives t such that arclength(subpath(0,t) of p) = a. Use direction t of path to obtain direction vector; directionpoint and directiontime convert between directions and parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpath cut operators: cutbefore and cutafter
rubrics_metrics.description: p1 cutbefore p2 is equivalent to subpath(xpart(p1 intersectiontimes p2), length(p1)) of p1 (but also sets cuttings). p1 cutafter p2 drops the part after the last intersection with p2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operators are convenient to trim paths at intersections; with multiple intersections they try to cut off as little as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joining lines: linejoin, linecap, and miterlimit
rubrics_metrics.description: linejoin controls how joints between segments are drawn (mitered, rounded, beveled). linecap controls end caps (butt, rounded, squared). miterlimit influences whether a mitered join becomes beveled when the limit threshold is crossed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set these internal variables before draw statements to change appearance. Example shows combinations of linejoin and linecap; use miterlimit to force bevel when acute angles make miters too long.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional statements syntax and semicolon rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic form: if condition: balanced tokens else: balanced tokens fi. else: if can be replaced with elseif (omit corresponding fi). Semicolons after statements inside if/else are optional except when building up a single statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using conditionals inside a single statement (e.g., draw p withcolor if cycle(p): red else: blue fi withpen pensquare;), do not add semicolons after the colour specifications; ensure the final semicolon marks the end of the statement. Use errmessage for error reporting and show for debugging output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relational and logical operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Relational operators: =, <>, <, <=, >, >=. Logical operators: and, or, not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build boolean expressions for conditions with these operators. Use not for negation and combine tests with and / or. Examples and truth-meaning are listed in a small table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional repetition via forever and exit clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost lacks built-in while/until loops; emulate them using forever: loop text endfor; and terminate with exitif boolean_expression or exitunless boolean_expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until loop: forever: loop text; exitif boolean_expression; endfor; While loop: forever: exitunless boolean_expression; loop text endfor. Use exitif/exitunless to break out of endless loops when condition holds/doesn't hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random number operators for stochastic drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: normaldeviate yields a standard normal random number; uniformdeviate yields uniform(0,arg).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to generate random points/walks (examples: Bernoulli walk using normaldeviate>0 as coin flip; vardef randompoint uses uniformdeviate to sample in rectangular region). Ensure you validate arguments when using uniformdeviate (e.g., r>l and u>b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Macros: def vs vardef, parameter types, and call-by-value
rubrics_metrics.description: def name = replacement text enddef defines a macro substitution; vardef name = replacement; returned_text enddef defines a macro that returns a value (like a function) and is grouped automatically. Formal parameter types include expr (expression) and text (sequence of tokens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vardef when you want to return a value without leaking intermediate variables. Parameters are call-by-value: occurrences of the formal parameter are replaced by the actual argument. Example: def rotatedaround(expr z,d)= shifted -z rotated d shifted z enddef; and vardef randompoint(expr l,r,b,u) = ... enddef;

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping and local variables: begingroup/endgroup and save
rubrics_metrics.description: Use begingroup ... endgroup to create a local scope so variable values inside the group don't affect outside. Use save name_sequence to make a variable local in name as well (protecting global names inside macros).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many macros/vardef definitions are auto-grouped. The save statement can be used inside or outside groups; outside a group it discards original values. Example macros: hide(text t) uses begingroup to run code silently; clearxy uses save x,y to clear names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicolon placement in vardef returns (pitfall)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a vardef, do not place a semicolon after the returned value (e.g., origin or (x,y)); placing a semicolon makes the return part of the hidden replacement text and can cause a runtime error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the returned expression is the last token before enddef without a trailing semicolon. The tutorial warns that adding a semicolon after origin or (x,y) in the randompoint vardef would break it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom operator/argument syntax definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: You can explicitly define argument syntax to construct unary, binary, or ternary operators via def/vardef mechanism and specific parameter types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page introduces that operator syntaxes can be defined (e.g., shows a pre-defined unary operator example just after this chunk). Use expr/text parameter types to control parsing and expansion behavior.
